call_points.text: Capex falls to ₹300-350 Cr in coming years, mostly domestic e-mobility, injection molding and lighting.
Debt reduction limited in FY27 by capex; significant cut expected by end-FY28 on free cash flow.
FY26 net new wins ~₹3,289 Cr annualised peak revenue, ~65% EV-related.
E-mobility is ~7.8% of revenue, largely one customer; a second customer is expected to SOP imminently.
Overseas electronics expected to reach EBITDA neutral by end-FY27 on strong order wins.
Overseas revenue fell as an existing customer unilaterally withdrew business; new programs began SOP in Q1FY27.
Management expects mid to high teen revenue growth for FY27.
FY27 capex is projected to be in the range of ₹450-500 crores, focused on EV, electronics, and lighting.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company, together with its Wholly Owned Subsidiary, VarrocCorp Holding B.V., Netherlands, has received an intimation from ICC International Court of Arbitration with respect to a Request for Arbitration initiated by OPmobility Lighting Holding, France (Erstwhile PO Lighting Systems). The request pertains to certain alleged breaches of covenants under the Securities Purchase Agreement executed between the parties on April 29, 2022, and subsequently amended on October 5, 2022, May 12, 2023, and June 15, 2023
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Opmobility Lighting Holding (“OP Mobility”) Plastic Omnium Group Company, a private limited liability company incorporated under the laws of France and registered with the Commercial and Companies Registry of Lyon under no. 908 521 651, having its registered offices at 19, boulevard Jules Carteret, 69007 Lyon, France.
tax_litigation.status: As intimated in our earlier filing dated 08-07-2025, OP Mobility filed its Request for Arbitration on June 27, 2025 for a claim amount of USD 66,405,802 plus legal cost). In the Statement of claim now received by the Company on February 10, 2026, the claim amount has been reduced to USD 25,380,960 and EUR 76,514.37 plus legal cost. The Company is evaluating the matter and intends to contest the claims and take appropriate steps including lodging counterclaims to protect its interests.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company’s Subsidiary in Romania also has an outstanding claim instituted in France against OPmobility Lighting Holding.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Opmobility Lighting Holding (“OP Mobility”) Plastic Omnium Group Company, a private limited liability company incorporated under the laws of France and registered with the Commercial and Companies Registry of Lyon under no. 908 521 651, having its registered offices at 19, boulevard Jules Carteret, 69007 Lyon, France.
tax_litigation.status: As intimated earlier, initially Varroc Electronics Romania S.R.L. (“VeR”) filed the claim against OP Mobility before Paris Commercial Court. Later, an appeal was filed by VeR against the judgement of Paris Commercial Court, seeking a claim of EURO 76 million plus other costs, meanwhile OP mobility has also filed an appeal/counterclaim.Financial implications, if any, will depend on the outcome of the proceedings. The Company is evaluating the matter and exploring legal and contractual remedies. It intends to consider further legal steps to protect its interests.

operating_notes.text: India Ratings upgraded Varroc Engineering's long-term bank loan facilities to IND AA+ with a stable outlook and affirmed short-term rating at IND A1+, while withdrawing NCD ratings following full repayment.
Varroc reported Q4FY26 revenue of ₹2,368.08 Cr (+12.8% YoY) and announced record annual net new business wins of ₹32,889 Cr.
Varroc signed a strategic cooperation arrangement with Suzhou Tolyy Optronics for localisation of digital cockpit and display solutions; the agreement specifies no cost and binds no volumes.
FY26 net new business wins were ~₹3,289 Cr in annualised peak revenue, ~65% related to EV models.
E-mobility contributed ~7.8% of revenue, largely from a single market-leading customer, with a second customer expected to SOP imminently.
FY26 India business revenue was ~₹8,000 Cr; overseas operations are targeted at ~₹4,000 Cr by FY31.
Forsee Power India FY26 turnover was ₹18.84 Cr and FY25 turnover was ₹10.57 Cr.
The Forsee Power India JV will initially make battery packs for three-wheelers, with a roadmap to two-wheelers, LCVs, buses, trucks, off-highway and industrial vehicles.

timeline.summary: India Ratings upgraded Varroc Engineering's long-term bank loan facilities to IND AA+/Stable on April 24, 2026.
On May 18, 2026, Varroc Engineering notified a board meeting on May 27, 2026 to approve audited FY26 results and consider a final FY26 dividend and a private-placement NCD issue.
Varroc Engineering Limited shared the audio recording link for its Investors/Conference Call on May 27, 2026, discussing audited financial results for Q4FY26 and FY26.
On June 2, 2026, Varroc Engineering filed the transcript of its Q4 and FY26 earnings conference call held on May 27, 2026.

On June 3, 2026, Varroc Engineering signed a strategic cooperation arrangement with Suzhou Tolyy Optronics to localise and supply digital cockpit and display solutions, with no cost or volume committed.

At its 38th AGM on 20 August 2026, Varroc guided FY27 revenue above ₹10,500 Cr (~20% growth) and set a ₹20,000 Cr FY31 revenue aspiration, with FY27 capex of ~₹550 Cr and debt reduction pushed to end-FY28.
2026-10-14: Varroc Engineering disclosed an RBI compounding order dated October 13, 2026 imposing ₹3.91 lakh for delay in repatriation of dues from a foreign entity under FEMA.
On 16 October 2026, Varroc Engineering announced the board approval to acquire a 45% stake in Forsee Power India for up to €4.5 million.

2026-10-16: Varroc Engineering said it will acquire a 45% stake in Forsee Power India, Forsee Power SA's battery-pack subsidiary, with management and operational control and an OCPRS subscription, subject to regulatory and corporate approvals.
